nodes.label: Generation-stamped event guard (poller vs GUI thread)
nodes.rationale: reader_start_nfc_phase() bumps a generation counter on every phase change so events still queued from a prior phase (scanner->poller transitions) are dropped rather than acted on twice, matching the repo-wide 'stale worker events' guard rule.

nodes.label: Step 0: Firmware/SDK Verification
nodes.rationale: Matching API major/minor does not guarantee ABI compatibility across firmware forks. A prior mismatch here wedged the device and produced a crash APPCHK did not catch, so the live device's hardware_target/firmware_origin_fork/firmware_commit/API version must be re-read and compared against the ufbt SDK before every build, not assumed stable from a previous session. Repeated verbatim (with per-app tables) for all three apps: universal_card_reader (L16-32), rfid_multi_reader (L499-513), subghz_auto_recorder (L659-678).

nodes.label: Fork ABI Drift (enum/struct layout not API-version-gated)
nodes.rationale: Momentum and other forks insert or append enum members / struct fields while leaving the reported API version unchanged (NfcProtocol gains Ntag4xx/Type4Tag/Emv shifting NfcProtocolNum 12->15 and NfcProtocolInvalid 13->16; LFRFIDProtocol inserts Indala224 mid-enum; MfClassicPollerMode inserts DictAttackCUID at id 3; MfClassicPollerEventDataKeyRequest inserts key_type before key_provided). A FAP that compiles in a *Invalid/*Num sentinel or a positional enum id can pass a shifted id to a firmware furi_check and crash/wedge the device. Fix: never compile in fork-sensitive sentinels; resolve relationships only through firmware-evaluated helpers (nfc_protocol_has_parent) against low, stable ids, or wrap fork-appended struct tails with reserved padding (SubRecPreset's fork_tail[4]).
nodes.norm_label: fork abi drift (enum/struct layout not api-version-gated)

nodes.label: GUI Thread Owns the Radio / View Model
nodes.rationale: Timer and worker callbacks run on TimersSrv or a worker thread, not the GUI thread. Calling with_view_model() from reader_phase_timer_callback() (TimersSrv thread) deadlocked against furi_timer_start() on the GUI thread, because both funnel through the same FreeRTOS timer command queue, freezing the app the moment any phase timer fired. Fix: callbacks off the GUI thread may only read plain fields (app->notice_active, app->gen) or post a custom event via view_dispatcher_send_custom_event(); every nfc_*/lfrfid_worker_* start/stop call, and every radio start/stop in subghz_auto_recorder, is issued from the GUI thread's custom-event handler in response to a posted event, never from the callback itself.
nodes.norm_label: gui thread owns the radio / view model

nodes.label: Async Worker Stop Is Not Synchronous
nodes.rationale: lfrfid_worker_stop() only sets a thread flag and returns immediately — the worker still holds the RF hardware after the call returns. Starting a second radio (e.g. NFC) right after can wedge the firmware hard enough to take USB down with it. Fix: use the joining variant (lfrfid_worker_stop_thread() -> furi_thread_join) before handing hardware to another radio, and re-create the worker thread when that phase starts again; the LF phase owns the LF worker thread's lifetime, never allocated once in app_alloc.
nodes.norm_label: async worker stop is not synchronous

nodes.label: Generation-Stamped Custom Events
nodes.rationale: Scanners/pollers re-detect in a loop, so a callback can fire repeatedly and several identical custom events queue up faster than the GUI thread drains them; acting on a stale duplicate after the app already moved to the next phase re-starts a poller on a running instance and hits a furi_check in nfc_start(). Fix: EVENT_MAKE(id, gen) packs app->gen into the event's high bits, app->gen++ on every phase change, and the handler drops any event whose generation doesn't match current — every custom event value must stay below 256 so the upper bits remain free for the generation. rfid_multi_reader applies the same idea via an explicit state guard (`if(app->state != RfidStateScanning) return true;`) on RfidEventDetected, since a duplicate can arrive after app->gen++ but still pass the gen check.

nodes.label: Colliding Radios / Strict Stop-Free-Start Ordering
nodes.rationale: NFC 13.56 MHz and LF 125 kHz hardware cannot be active at once, so every app alternates timed phases and must guarantee only one radio is ever up: universal_card_reader funnels every radio-touching entry point through reader_stop_all() first; rfid_multi_reader's rfid_stop_all() calls every registered backend's scan_stop(), not just the active one, as the sole guarantee two radios never overlap. Violating the ordering wedges the firmware.

nodes.label: Stack Sizing By Measurement, Not Guess
nodes.rationale: An undersized stack surfaces as an opaque furi_check/HardFault, not a clear error, so stack_size is set from measured `top` Stack Min headroom rather than guessed. Stack Min is a FreeRTOS high-water mark (furi_thread_get_stack_space) that only ever falls, so one `top` sampled at the end of a continuous session (app never relaunched) covers every code path that session executed; a reading from a stale, pre-reflash binary is explicitly not combined with a fresh one. Concrete values: universal_card_reader stack_size 12*1024 with Stack Min 11080-11216/12284 across Save/Load cycles; rfid_multi_reader stack_size 8*1024 with Stack Min 7424-7692/8188; subghz_auto_recorder stack_size 12*1024 with Stack Min 11288-11444/12284 even through a real capture+replay cycle — each comfortably clears the roughly 4096-byte pass bar the project uses as its margin threshold.
nodes.norm_label: stack sizing by measurement, not guess

nodes.label: CLI Debug Loop (cap.py + live log/top streams)
nodes.rationale: `top` and `log <level>` are both live, continuously-refreshing streams that never return to the CLI prompt, so any --cmd queued after one in the same cap.py invocation is silently dropped rather than executed — every triggering `input send` must be queued before attaching log/top, never after. `loader close` is not always a reliable recovery (it cannot interrupt a GUI thread genuinely blocked inside a synchronous SDK call, confirmed live during an Emulate hang); `power reboot` over the CLI recovers even that case. This CLI-only, hard-deadline capture discipline (build -> launch -> capture -> find furi_check/[E] -> fix -> repeat) is why cap.py exists as a standalone pyserial helper rather than an interactive session: an interactive `cli` session hangs the terminal.
nodes.norm_label: cli debug loop (cap.py + live log/top streams)

nodes.label: Mandatory Two-Pass Review (flipper-c-review + flipper-perf-review)
nodes.rationale: Every task that writes or changes C ends with two review passes in a fixed order — correctness/design/failure-mode review, then stack/memory/thread/redraw-cost review — run after ufbt is warning-clean and after any on-device verification but before the commit message, because reviewing from memory instead of invoking the skills misses the project's own catalog of prior real crashes (fork-ABI, GUI-thread, async-stop, generation-stamping) that motivated the other rules in this file.

nodes.label: Ethical/Legal Use Notice
nodes.rationale: Only read, record, or replay devices/signals the user owns or is explicitly authorised to test; unauthorized reading/recording of other people's cards or RF transmissions is a legal violation in most countries. Governs all three FAPs in the repo since each one reads or transmits over radio.

nodes.label: EMV Read Diagnosis (universal_card_reader)
nodes.rationale: Dated 2026-08-01, before emv.c existed: establishes that the app's NFC path deliberately downgrades any card to its ISO14443-3 transport protocol via protocol_base() (nfc_protocol_has_parent), so it polls only an ISO14443-3a poller and never reaches the ISO14443-4 APDU layer — the UID it reports for a bank card is a random per-tap UID, not a usable identifier. Confirms the pinned stock SDK exposes iso14443_4a_poller_send_block (the APDU pipe, callable only from inside the poller callback) but ships no EMV/TLV/APDU helper at all, and that Momentum's fork-only EMV protocol id is unlinkable from a FAP built against the stock SDK — so a minimal BER-TLV decoder had to be written from scratch. This diagnosis is the direct design origin of emv.c/emv.h.

nodes.label: Proposed EMV APDU Read Chain (PPSE->AID->GPO->READ RECORD)
nodes.rationale: Read-only APDU command chain proposed for emv_read(): SELECT PPSE (2PAY.SYS.DDF01) to collect AIDs -> SELECT the first AID answering 9000 -> read its 9F38 PDOL and build GPO data with standard terminal defaults -> GET PROCESSING OPTIONS -> walk the AFL (format 1 or 2) with READ RECORD, harvesting PAN/expiry/name/track-2/label -> optionally GET DATA 9F4F + READ RECORD the transaction log. Every field not returned by the card prints 'not disclosed' rather than being treated as a read failure, since withholding the PAN over contactless is common and expected, not an app defect.
nodes.norm_label: proposed emv apdu read chain (ppse->aid->gpo->read record)
